summary: The tests compile and use Playwright APIs correctly with awaited assertions. Test case IDs are preserved in titles. Selectors use role-based selectors which is good, but hardcoded assumptions about product count and page title reduce flexibility. URL and title assertions are adequate but could be more thorough. The usage of expect(products) for a collection count is correct. The baseUrl is a specific test URL, not a placeholder. No hardcoded waits or invalid API usage detected. The locator usage is correct; no direct iteration over locators. Some assumptions in selectors and expected counts pose risks for maintainability and reliability.

issues.description: Selectors assume the presence and label of the 'Electronics' link and that products have the class 'product-item'. These selectors may be brittle if UI changes.
issues.recommendation: Use data-testid attributes or more robust selectors if possible to make tests less fragile.

issues.description: The test TC-002 asserts the page title equals 'Electronics' but this assumes the page title directly matches the category name without further validation.
issues.recommendation: Consider validating the title includes additional context if applicable, to prevent false positives.

issues.description: Test TC-003 assumes exactly 4 products are in the Electronics category which is hardcoded and reduces test flexibility.
issues.recommendation: Make product counts configurable or verify product relevance via content instead of count alone.

recommendations: Introduce stable data attributes in the UI to enhance selector robustness.
Avoid hardcoding product counts to improve test flexibility and reliability.
Enhance assertions on page titles to confirm page identity more clearly.
Consider adding tests for negative scenarios and boundary cases in product listings.
